programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is at Wallyford recycling centre on Scotland's east coast hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. He enlists the help of signwriter Joel Poole for a creative design on a glass-fronted cabinet, whilst upcycler Sarah Peterson turns her attention to a radical makeover on an old wicker trunk. Meanwhile, JJ sets himself the challenge of turning a pair of wooden doors into a potential profit.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The beautiful Wye Valley may not be too far from Bristol, where today’s couple are from, but it’s a whole world away in terms of lifestyle. Steve Brown has some tempting properties up his sleeve, and during some downtime, all three manage to unwind and enjoy the scenery with a leisurely canoe ride on the River Wye itself.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice

In Liverpool, Gail Caldwell faces two cars heading the wrong way down a motorway slip road, while another driver runs a red light with a pedestrian on the crossing. Dashcams capture all the evidence investigators need to get justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is just outside Swansea in the suburb of Sketty to see a very characterful three-bedroom semi with great original features. He’s also in Ilfracombe in north Devon, where a two-bedroom dwelling does not create the greatest of first impressions. Tommy is in London on the peninsula of the Isle of dogs, where a three-bedroom flat has great potential as a development opportunity.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.desc: BBC Children in Need brings the nation together for a spectacular evening of entertainment, warmth and sparkle, with more than a sprinkle of Hollywood stardust. Live from MediaCityUK in Salford, hosts Mel Giedroyc, Sara Cox, Alex Jones, Rylan and Tyler West lead a star-studded show packed with famous faces, dazzling performances, exclusive sketches and big surprises. Highlights on the night include special collaborations with much-loved BBC shows, plus the heartwarming return of the Children in Need Choir, who sing a special medley live. Alongside the glitz and glamour, inspiring stories from children and young people across the UK highlight the life-changing impact of BBC Children in Need.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A driver pulls out to overtake a van near Wrexham, and collides head-on with an oncoming car. The van's camera captures the devastating impact, and a witness recounts the shocking aftermath. On another country road, a risky overtake brings a car face-to-face with a lorry. An insurer untangles a disputed roundabout crash, while tests in Caerphilly reveal the terrifying forces unleashed in a collision.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is at Wallyford recycling centre on Scotland's east coast hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. He enlists the help of signwriter Joel Poole for a creative design on a glass-fronted cabinet, whilst upcycler Sarah Peterson turns her attention to a radical makeover on an old wicker trunk. Meanwhile, JJ sets himself the challenge of turning a pair of wooden doors into a potential profit.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The beautiful Wye Valley may not be too far from Bristol, where today’s couple are from, but it’s a whole world away in terms of lifestyle. Steve Brown has some tempting properties up his sleeve, and during some downtime, all three manage to unwind and enjoy the scenery with a leisurely canoe ride on the River Wye itself.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: Two drivers stage a crash and pursue a £60,000 insurance payout. But they overlook one crucial detail: the dashcam records their scheming as well as the smash. In Liverpool, Gail Caldwell faces two cars heading the wrong way down a motorway slip road, while another driver runs a red light with a pedestrian on the crossing. Dashcams capture all the evidence investigators need to get justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is just outside Swansea in the suburb of Sketty to see a very characterful three-bedroom semi with great original features. He’s also in Ilfracombe in north Devon, where a two-bedroom dwelling does not create the greatest of first impressions. Tommy is in London on the peninsula of the Isle of dogs, where a three-bedroom flat has great potential as a development opportunity.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.desc: A driver pulls out to overtake a van near Wrexham, and collides head-on with an oncoming car. The van's camera captures the devastating impact, and a witness recounts the shocking aftermath. On another country road, a risky overtake brings a car face-to-face with a lorry. An insurer untangles a disputed roundabout crash, while tests in Caerphilly reveal the terrifying forces unleashed in a collision.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Amongst the heavy industrial landscape lie some surprising pockets of nature and a bustling marina. programme.title: Honey

Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: The Bidding Room

Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. programme.title: Honey

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A driver pulls out to overtake a van near Wrexham, and collides head-on with an oncoming car. The van's camera captures the devastating impact, and a witness recounts the shocking aftermath. On another country road, a risky overtake brings a car face-to-face with a lorry. An insurer untangles a disputed roundabout crash, while tests in Caerphilly reveal the terrifying forces unleashed in a collision.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

programme.title: BBC News at One

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers is at Wallyford recycling centre on Scotland's east coast hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. He enlists the help of signwriter Joel Poole for a creative design on a glass-fronted cabinet, whilst upcycler Sarah Peterson turns her attention to a radical makeover on an old wicker trunk. Meanwhile, JJ sets himself the challenge of turning a pair of wooden doors into a potential profit.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The beautiful Wye Valley may not be too far from Bristol, where today’s couple are from, but it’s a whole world away in terms of lifestyle. Steve Brown has some tempting properties up his sleeve, and during some downtime, all three manage to unwind and enjoy the scenery with a leisurely canoe ride on the River Wye itself.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Ollie, Gus, Benjy and Joe – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Dashcams capture all the evidence investigators need to get justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is just outside Swansea in the suburb of Sketty to see a very characterful three-bedroom semi with great original features. He’s also in Ilfracombe in north Devon, where a two-bedroom dwelling does not create the greatest of first impressions. Tommy is in London on the peninsula of the Isle of dogs, where a three-bedroom flat has great potential as a development opportunity.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.desc: BBC Children in Need brings the nation together for a spectacular evening of entertainment, warmth and sparkle, with more than a sprinkle of Hollywood stardust. Highlights on the night include special collaborations with much-loved BBC shows, plus the heartwarming return of the Children in Need Choir, who sing a special medley live. The One Show Challenge Squad take centre stage again as new recruits Zoe and Serena tackle epic challenges to help make a difference to other young lives. Radio 2's Owain Wyn Evans is live in the studio for a hero's welcome after completing his gruelling 400-mile four nations cycle challenge in aid of this year’s appeal. Alongside the glitz and glamour, inspiring stories from children and young people across the UK highlight the life-changing impact of BBC Children in Need.

programme.title: Honey

She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: This surprising grand tour follows the river Ythan in rural Aberdeenshire, which flows through a landscape of wheat fields and haunted castles and on to a coast rich in wildlife. On the way, Paul Murton learns how to make a haystack, speak the local 'Doric' and has a ghostly encounter with a woman in Fyvie Castle. He visits Gight Castle, the ruined home of poet Lord Byron’s family. Journey’s end is at the mouth of the river, where sand dunes have created Scotland’s version of the Sahara.

programme.title: Landward

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: A knife attack in Inverness leads police to a volatile suspect and a house packed with blades, from Samurai swords to machetes and zombie knives. Released on bail while police await DNA results, he is soon wanted over another violent attack. On the Isle of Skye, rescuers race to find a climber who has been missing for three days in the mountains. And near Fort William, an American tourist has an unusual concern after a crash.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Deep in the Highlands, Loch Morar is home to a mysterious legend: Morag, a creature said to lurk beneath its dark, cold waters. Comedian and ecologist Zara Gladman teams up with parapsychologist Evelyn Hollow to investigate the sightings and meet locals whose accounts have kept the story alive for generations. A loch superintendent recalls a strange wake racing across the water, an angler describes three huge humps rising behind his boat, and a lifelong monster hunter reveals how easily shadows can fool even experts. As Zara gathers environmental DNA from the loch, could science finally offer an explanation? The results point to a familiar inhabitant: the European eel. But can it account for everything witnesses claim to have seen? With scepticism, humour and a healthy dose of curiosity, Zara and Evelyn dive into the mystery of Morag, and ask whether this elusive monster is real, misunderstood, or best left to legend.

programme.title: Mythland

programme.title: Street Gangs

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Ex gang member and best-selling author Graeme Armstrong explores the underbelly of Dundee as he speaks to ex gang members in local schemes Whitfield and Kirkton and tries to understand the causes of recent civil unrest in the area. programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Best-selling author and reformed gang member Graeme Armstrong explores how to escape the gang life. How do ‘young team’ members turn their lives around? Is it even possible? In this episode, Graeme explains that there were only ever three options he could see: death, prison or redemption. This time focusing on Glasgow, Graeme explores the Wyndford Scheme in Maryhill and travels to Glencoe to meet a man who, like himself, managed to turn his life around and leave gangs behind for good.

programme.title: Stevens & McCarthy
programme.desc: Stevens & McCarthy are back with their collection of comic characters, spoofs and musical comedy. At the roll van, Davie is not happy with the chat, a gamer mum loses her cool, and the girls think twinkly lights are the answer to all life's woes.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Ex-Buzzcocks drummer John Maher shares punk memories and his current photography obsession, from his adopted home on the Isle of Harris. We hear how John toured the world supporting the Sex Pistols, and he opens up his scrapbooks to reveal meeting heroes such as Blondie’s Debbie Harry. Having lived a fast-paced life, John moved to Harris 20 years ago, and where he soon picked up his dusty camera and turned his lens to his adopted home. John aims to depict the island in a new way, with the focus not just on the breathtaking landscapes, but also the people and places left behind by humans. We join him as he completes his current project, which features a series of photographs focusing on a local family transforming an old croft into their perfect new home.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Rehab centres are treating some of their youngest-ever and most physically damaged addicts, and ketamine has been their drug of choice. Stacey Dooley gains rare access to a rehab in Stockport and gets to know former users. Many are in chronic pain, and one young man needs bladder reconstruction surgery. Over four months, she follows them through recovery, relationships, setbacks and celebrations.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey follows three Ukrainian civilians training with British soldiers to fight Russia. In just five weeks, a florist, a welder and a jeweller learn to 'survive and be lethal'.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Khalil never remembers his dates’ names, so he calls them all 'baby girl' to skirt around it. Obsessed with looking good, he checks himself out in the reflection of a spoon every 20 minutes on dinner dates and thinks it’s impressive to tell boastful, drunken stories. No wonder the ladies don’t come back for a second date! Cavan is fed up of his best mate Khalil’s dating fails and Khalil not listening to his advice, so he calls on the help of Gen Z's most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to put this 21-year-old Notts boy on the spot and get him to own up to his bad dating habits. Khalil and Oloni watch video feedback from some very honest friends and exes to show him first hand where it's all going wrong, before Oloni sets Khalil up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to turn him from a bad date to a good date. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Cavan, can Khalil stop calling his dates 'baby girl', can he resist the urge to check himself out and will he take Oloni's advice on board and stop telling laddish, drunken stories?

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Larisa is fed up of hearing about her best mate Dami’s latest in a long line of dating fails. He walks out mid-date, interrogates and pulls girls up on their outfits, music choices and lifestyle, and thinks they’re lucky to have him! It’s time for an intervention, so Larisa enlists the help of Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert Oloni to put the 24-year-old Londoner on the spot and help him own up to his disastrous dating habits. Oloni reviews his dating past and gives him a cold, hard dose of reality as she and Dami watch some honest and sometimes surprising video feedback from family members, friends and even exes to show him where it’s all going wrong. Oloni sets Dami up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to shake off his bad habits and hopefully become a better dater. As Oloni and Larisa watch on, can Dami ditch the interrogation act, stop being so rude to his dates and actually stay to the end?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.desc: Recovering from her injuries, Katniss is recruited into the Star Squad, whose mission is to produce propaganda. Katniss will not miss this opportunity for revenge on President Snow.

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum
programme.desc: At 11 years old, Alex vanished on holiday with his mother and grandfather for six years. Now, he's retracing his steps across Europe to tell the full story for the first time.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy, Richard and James attempt to save the planet by building their own electric car and then put their latest 'green' creation through the rigours of the new car testing process. The Star in a Reasonably Priced Car is Frost/Nixon and The Damned United star Michael Sheen.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Wrong Trousers
programme.desc: Oscar-winning animated adventure featuring Wallace and Gromit. The duo are plunged into a hilarious tale of skulduggery involving an extraordinary pair of automated trousers and a villainous penguin. Featuring Peter Sallis as the voice of Wallace.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Humphrey and his team are baffled by a set of reverse burglaries where items are left behind rather than taken. With their only credible suspect being Santa, it’s a race against time to find the real culprit in time for Christmas. The only clues are a pile of ash and glove fibres at each location. With four open cases counting against them, and police HQ breathing down their necks, the team are up against it. They must figure out how the victims are connected, catch the person responsible and save the station in time for the festivities. But when the team make a breakthrough with an unexpected connection to 1973, it’s a bittersweet discovery that makes them reconsider the true meaning of Christmas.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Whilst home alone watching family videos, Bob encounters a surprise visitor - his late wife’s ghost, Linda, who has a haunting demand: get out. When there’s a second unsettling encounter and writing on a mirror, Humphrey and the team are called in to investigate. Esther is deeply sceptical, but Humphrey is more than happy to dive into his first haunting. Surely there’s a rational explanation?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It may be a time for peace and goodwill, but there is trouble brewing in the Brown household this Christmas. Cathy takes exception to having her mother opening her mail and instigates a clever plan for revenge. Agnes is shocked when the annual Nativity play is cancelled. She vows to stage her own Christmas play. The new priest puts his foot down - but nobody gets in the way of Agnes Brown.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has finally been given permission to stage her own Nativity play and is determined to put on the greatest show on Earth. The only thing standing in her way now is local priest Father Damien, who is insisting that Agnes makes some last-minute changes to her rather unusual script. Will Agnes ever get to play the Virgin Mary?

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: A festive trip down memory lane prompts Pat to question his very identity. The ghosts come up with a surprise Christmas present for Alison, whose family lunch does not go to plan.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: It’s coming up to Christmas, and Mike’s mum is staying. Betty wants to be helpful, but it isn’t long before she is driving Mike and Alison round the bend. Betty has overstayed her welcome, but Alison and Mike don’t quite have the heart to tell her. Just as she decides to leave of her own volition, Betty suspects something is terribly wrong at Button House. She adopts extreme measures to make the house safe and in doing so endangers the resident Ghosts – will they come out of this unscathed?

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. programme.desc: Rehab centres are treating some of their youngest-ever and most physically damaged addicts, and ketamine has been their drug of choice. Over four months, she follows them through recovery, relationships, setbacks and celebrations.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey follows three Ukrainian civilians training with British soldiers to fight Russia. In just five weeks, a florist, a welder and a jeweller learn to 'survive and be lethal'.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Khalil never remembers his dates’ names, so he calls them all 'baby girl' to skirt around it. Obsessed with looking good, he checks himself out in the reflection of a spoon every 20 minutes on dinner dates and thinks it’s impressive to tell boastful, drunken stories. No wonder the ladies don’t come back for a second date! Cavan is fed up of his best mate Khalil’s dating fails and Khalil not listening to his advice, so he calls on the help of Gen Z's most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to put this 21-year-old Notts boy on the spot and get him to own up to his bad dating habits. Khalil and Oloni watch video feedback from some very honest friends and exes to show him first hand where it's all going wrong, before Oloni sets Khalil up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to turn him from a bad date to a good date. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Cavan, can Khalil stop calling his dates 'baby girl', can he resist the urge to check himself out and will he take Oloni's advice on board and stop telling laddish, drunken stories?

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Larisa is fed up of hearing about her best mate Dami’s latest in a long line of dating fails. He walks out mid-date, interrogates and pulls girls up on their outfits, music choices and lifestyle, and thinks they’re lucky to have him! It’s time for an intervention, so Larisa enlists the help of Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert Oloni to put the 24-year-old Londoner on the spot and help him own up to his disastrous dating habits. Oloni reviews his dating past and gives him a cold, hard dose of reality as she and Dami watch some honest and sometimes surprising video feedback from family members, friends and even exes to show him where it’s all going wrong. Oloni sets Dami up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to shake off his bad habits and hopefully become a better dater. As Oloni and Larisa watch on, can Dami ditch the interrogation act, stop being so rude to his dates and actually stay to the end?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.desc: Recovering from her injuries, Katniss is recruited into the Star Squad, whose mission is to produce propaganda. Katniss will not miss this opportunity for revenge on President Snow.

programme.title: Kidnapped by My Mum

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Wrong Trousers
programme.desc: Oscar-winning animated adventure featuring Wallace and Gromit. The duo are plunged into a hilarious tale of skulduggery involving an extraordinary pair of automated trousers and a villainous penguin. Featuring Peter Sallis as the voice of Wallace.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Humphrey and his team are baffled by a set of reverse burglaries where items are left behind rather than taken. With their only credible suspect being Santa, it’s a race against time to find the real culprit in time for Christmas. The only clues are a pile of ash and glove fibres at each location. With four open cases counting against them, and police HQ breathing down their necks, the team are up against it. They must figure out how the victims are connected, catch the person responsible and save the station in time for the festivities. But when the team make a breakthrough with an unexpected connection to 1973, it’s a bittersweet discovery that makes them reconsider the true meaning of Christmas.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Whilst home alone watching family videos, Bob encounters a surprise visitor - his late wife’s ghost, Linda, who has a haunting demand: get out. When there’s a second unsettling encounter and writing on a mirror, Humphrey and the team are called in to investigate. Esther is deeply sceptical, but Humphrey is more than happy to dive into his first haunting. Surely there’s a rational explanation?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It may be a time for peace and goodwill, but there is trouble brewing in the Brown household this Christmas. Cathy takes exception to having her mother opening her mail and instigates a clever plan for revenge. Agnes is shocked when the annual Nativity play is cancelled. She vows to stage her own Christmas play. The new priest puts his foot down - but nobody gets in the way of Agnes Brown.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has finally been given permission to stage her own Nativity play and is determined to put on the greatest show on Earth. The only thing standing in her way now is local priest Father Damien, who is insisting that Agnes makes some last-minute changes to her rather unusual script. Will Agnes ever get to play the Virgin Mary?

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: A festive trip down memory lane prompts Pat to question his very identity. The ghosts come up with a surprise Christmas present for Alison, whose family lunch does not go to plan.

programme.title: Ghosts
programme.desc: It’s coming up to Christmas, and Mike’s mum is staying. Betty wants to be helpful, but it isn’t long before she is driving Mike and Alison round the bend. Betty has overstayed her welcome, but Alison and Mike don’t quite have the heart to tell her. Just as she decides to leave of her own volition, Betty suspects something is terribly wrong at Button House. She adopts extreme measures to make the house safe and in doing so endangers the resident Ghosts – will they come out of this unscathed?

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
