programme.desc: Brinicle invites Pancake onto his radio show but is cross when his accidental burps prove a hit. Pancake soon discovers that fame as ‘burping guy’ has its downsides.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad and Cosima both think they're the best at pranking. Their prank war quickly spirals out of control, until Big Lizard finally reveals Proxima's real pranking champion!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's bathtime! The ducklings are determined Weasy will get clean.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The Gnome Crystal Mine has ground to a halt, leaving the forest with no crystals, no power supply and melting ice lollies! The heroes are tasked with a quest to find out what has happened and to fix it. It turns out that a slimy beast named Smarg has made the mine her home. But with Hoofius’s fear of gunk getting the better of him, evicting the slippery Smarg is not going to be easy.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings use magic Chinese lanterns for sound and light shows.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a referee at a football match, and Frog sees how much a footballer is cheered for scoring a goal. He is desperate to score one himself, but can he get past Duck's red card?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko worries that Hattrem could be holding itself back for the sake of others.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The dark magic of Vexius has contaminated Alfea with a lethal residue. The Winx, together with Flora's parents, are searching for a cure to save the flora and fauna of the magic kingdom.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini and Abby go head-to-head in an epic Children in Need racing challenge, and Tyler West and Hacker make some delicious Pudsey Pizzas.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve seeks out deadly creatures in miniature, including Australia’s most beautiful spider, Oman’s deadly deathstalker scorpion and a bright blue beauty in Indonesia.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens, this time in south east Asia. Since the 19th century, western gardeners have loved tropical gardens. Monty visits the archetype - the mysterious Jim Thompson's Garden in Bangkok. He seeks something more authentic in the Royal Palace gardens and the floating gardens of the canals of Bangkok. In Bali, his preconceptions are challenged again. Is the western picture of the exotic garden a construct?

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: In a rare in-depth interview, Sir Rod Stewart and Penny Lancaster welcome Anita Rani into their home to discuss their lives, family, fame and faith, and how Christmases past and present have shaped them. Across an intimate fireside chat, Christmas crafting in a festive greenhouse and a stroll around the stunning grounds of their countryside home, they reflect on Rod’s rise to fame, Penny’s journey from model to special constable and festive traditions, including exchanging gifts with Elton John.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off some sensational breakfasts to kickstart your weekend, including granola and yoghurt cupcakes, a banana and peanut butter bake, and a crazy-but-delicious breakfast pizza.

programme.title: Ice Cold in Alex
programme.desc: During the German offensive in Libya in 1942, Captain Anson, commander of a motor ambulance convoy, finds himself cut off from his unit with only an old ambulance to take him back to Alexandria. His companions are two young nurses and his sergeant, Tom Pugh. As the little party sets off on the long journey, they meet Van der Poel, a South African captain who begs a lift.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: In Nottingham, we see a Victorian town house with an unusual back garden, a couple hope to transform a dilapidated mid-terrace in Bournemouth, and a one-bedroom flat becomes an ultra-modern two-bedroom in north London. Dion, Martin and Tommy meet the successful bidders as we follow three unique renovations.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage as Wales take on Norway in Oslo for their penultimate game in the Nations League.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Stephen Watson presents full match coverage from Windsor Park as Northern Ireland take on Ukraine in the Nations League. With just two matches remaining, Northern Ireland remain firmly in contention for promotion from League B. However, Ukraine could provide a major test as Michael O’Neill’s side look to bolster their position ahead of a potentially decisive final fixture. Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, with expert analysis from Stuart Dallas, Caragh Hamilton and David Healy.

programme.title: 40 Hits of 1975 at the BBC
programme.desc: Take a musical trip back in time with 40 essential hits from the year 1975, plucked from the BBC’s archives. The punk explosion was two years away, and disco was only just starting to surface, but these 12 months were still packed with classic songs that remain staples to this day. Key moments include ABBA in Blackpool on Seaside Special, the Bay City Rollers riding the wave of Rollermania, and debut hits from key artists who were pioneers in their individual genres, including Bob Marley, Supertramp and Kraftwerk.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The remaining five chefs return to the kitchen for two demanding challenges that will push their skills, creativity and ambition to the limit as they battle for a place in the quarter-final.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the end of an era on Gardeners' World as Monty approaches his final programme from Longmeadow, the garden he has shared with the nation for the last 16 years. With Ned by his side, he celebrates the enduring pleasures of gardening and serves up one last bulb lasagne. Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson goes back to school, Flower School, to learn how to make a unique, living flower wreath.

programme.title: The Battle of the River Plate
programme.desc: Second World War naval adventure based on the true story of the pursuit of the seemingly unstoppable German battleship Graf Spee. Allied forces chase the vessel all the way to South America, but after several failed attempts to sink the enemy ship, the Allies find themselves hatching a desperate and audacious plan.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team step back in time at the Beamish Open Air Museum near Newcastle. Amongst the items brought to light are a rare rapier sword allegedly smuggled out of Russia in the props box of the Bolshoi Ballet. We meet a keen collector of battlefield finds known as trench art, and the finest music box to appear on the Roadshow is valued.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the place sometimes dubbed 'the last bastion of free speech in the western world' - the historic Oxford Union. Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at the local auction house. Christina uncovers a famous fake while Mark gets a religious education after discovering a rare Baptist bust. Paul delves into the history of the auction site which is built on top of infamous Greenham Common.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor serves up more unmissable action from the world of Strictly as she chats to more couples about their weekend preparations. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill gives an exclusive look at some of her newest creations.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Fridges have been quietly ‘keeping things cool’ in the kitchen for over 100 years, and yet most of us barely give them a second thought. Hannah hits the production line with appliance giants Bosch to find the lifeblood at the heart of every fridge and gets a lesson in carrot droop. And she takes a long, cool look at the fridge’s history to reveal how a French monk with a flair for chemistry, a 17th century chicken incubator and an explosive invention in Australia created the ultimate chill.

programme.title: The Emerald Isles
programme.desc: From mighty, windswept cliffs to lush, sub-tropical gardens, the islands off the west coast of Ireland are extraordinary in their diversity. On the Aran Islands, Ardal learns from a practising monk of their ancient Christian heritage while, all around, a remarkable range of flora blooms, encouraged by traditional farming methods. Continuing south, Ardal visits the abandoned Great Blasket Island, former home to Irish author Peig Sayers, now home to a thriving seal colony and two young caretakers. On nearby Valentia Island, Ardal is shown fossilised evidence of early life emerging from the sea, while in the surrounding waters, oyster conservationists are hard at work. On land, Ireland’s only vermouth producers forage for ingredients. The episode ends with a visit to spectacular Skellig Michael, a UNESCO world heritage site that’s home to numerous puffins and the world’s most dramatic ancient monastery.

programme.title: Suzie Lee's Great Food Made Simple
programme.desc: Suzie visits Artis in Londonderry and is inspired to make a sticky toffee soufflé.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Marco chases three Michelin stars, Gordon breaks away to build his own name, and Heston rewrites the rules as huge success brings both fame and a new world of pressure.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O’Connell.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: The Peelers are back. While patrolling Belfast city centre, Dave and Owen stop a suspected drug dealer. They find a wad of cash and cocaine. The man claims he is a drug user struggling with addiction and, from the back of a cell, tells Stephen about his life. But when speaking to the custody sergeant, he lets slip a crucial detail that confirms Dave’s suspicions. Next, reports come in of two men fighting on the street – each claiming to be the victim. After speaking to eyewitnesses and CCTV operators, Anna brings both into custody. On the way, one of the men launches a torrent of abuse at the Peelers. In west Belfast, the vehicle crime team – Dennis and Chris - are on shift and notice a car being driven erratically round a bend. When stopped, the driver, who is known to the team, tries to charm his way out of trouble.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul fishes at the famous Bridge Pool near Christchurch in Dorset, hoping to catch sea trout. Bob arrives late but redeems himself by hooking the first fish of the day. After a glorious morning, Paul persuades Bob to charter a boat out to sea in search of sea bass. Bob has a history of sea sickness and is not keen, but eventually they venture out to the Needles, where Paul makes an incredible catch. The fish is too big for Bob to handle, so they head off to a local restaurant to prepare it. Bob performs a small cameo as an irritating waiter.

programme.title: Joins BBC News
programme.desc: BBC One joins the BBC's rolling news channel for a night of news.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the northernmost reaches of the UK – Shetland – to fish the lochs and the seas of this remote and beautiful place for trout and pollock. Shetland is an archipelago of about 100 islands off the north east coast of Scotland, only around 15 of which are inhabited. It feels like they have entered a very different world - and it's full of surprises for both of them.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Bioacoustics technology and AI have allowed scientists to not only decode complex animal sound data but also begin communicating with animals. While this may mean the salvation of countless animal species, the advent of inter-species communication could also have far-reaching risks for the ecosystem. In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Calum Clunie has been growing for the Fife veg and flower shows since he was 15 years old, and now he has an allotment in Leven that has dedicated to growing the largest leeks and most dazzling dahlias. Throughout a growing season, Calum let us in on his show-growing secrets as he grows giant onions and massive cabbages alongside stunning sweet peas and delightful dahlias. As a fitting end to the growing year, Calum hosts his own homegrown show in his grandparent’s back garden. It's a real family affair, and there is a visit from a special surprise judge.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team enter Border country as the Roadshow visits Manderston, near Berwick-upon-Tweed. Amongst the items featured are pieces from Queen Victoria's household, a gruesome man trap and Lord Palmer's collection of rare biscuit tins.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Rochester Cathedral in Kent. Antiques expert Elizabeth Talbot falls for a book of fairy tales illustrated by Arthur Rackham, and Adam Partridge discovers an elegant chiming Swiss pocket watch. Presenter Paul Martin meets one of the last remaining survivors of the Dunkirk evacuation during the Second World War.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives as she’s joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the couple’s next dances.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage from Hampden as Scotland host North Macedonia in the Nations League.

programme.title: Die Hard with a Vengeance
programme.desc: Classic action blockbuster. John McClane (Bruce Willis) and a store owner, Zeus (Samuel L Jackson), must play a bomber's deadly game as they race around New York trying to stop him.

programme.title: Blue Story
programme.desc: A feature adaptation of Rapman's YouTube series about two young south London friends from different boroughs and their deepening relationships with gangs and girls.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: Desperate to recover their losses, the Phelans strike a deal with Ozzie Thompson. At Jamie and Melissa’s engagement party, Michael and Diana attempt to broker peace with the family. Meanwhile, Freddie spirals further out of Michael’s control.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and asks if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. As the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

Dion, Martin and Tommy meet the successful bidders as we follow three unique renovations.

programme.title: Flog It!

programme.title: UEFA Nations League

programme.title: UEFA Nations League

Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, with expert analysis from Stuart Dallas, Caragh Hamilton and David Healy.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It’s the end of an era on Gardeners' World as Monty approaches his final programme from Longmeadow, the garden he has shared with the nation for the last 16 years. With Ned by his side, he celebrates the enduring pleasures of gardening and serves up one last bulb lasagne. Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson goes back to school, Flower School, to learn how to make a unique, living flower wreath.

programme.title: The Battle of the River Plate
programme.desc: Second World War naval adventure based on the true story of the pursuit of the seemingly unstoppable German battleship Graf Spee. Allied forces chase the vessel all the way to South America, but after several failed attempts to sink the enemy ship, the Allies find themselves hatching a desperate and audacious plan.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team step back in time at the Beamish Open Air Museum near Newcastle. Amongst the items brought to light are a rare rapier sword allegedly smuggled out of Russia in the props box of the Bolshoi Ballet. We meet a keen collector of battlefield finds known as trench art, and the finest music box to appear on the Roadshow is valued.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the place sometimes dubbed 'the last bastion of free speech in the western world' - the historic Oxford Union. Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at the local auction house. Christina uncovers a famous fake while Mark gets a religious education after discovering a rare Baptist bust. Paul delves into the history of the auction site which is built on top of infamous Greenham Common.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor serves up more unmissable action from the world of Strictly as she chats to more couples about their weekend preparations. Also, costume designer Vicky Gill gives an exclusive look at some of her newest creations.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Fridges have been quietly ‘keeping things cool’ in the kitchen for over 100 years, and yet most of us barely give them a second thought. Hannah hits the production line with appliance giants Bosch to find the lifeblood at the heart of every fridge and gets a lesson in carrot droop. And she takes a long, cool look at the fridge’s history to reveal how a French monk with a flair for chemistry, a 17th century chicken incubator and an explosive invention in Australia created the ultimate chill.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The standout chefs from the week’s heats battle it out again in the quarter-final. The stakes are higher, the challenges more demanding, and the judges’ expectations are greater than ever.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Marco chases three Michelin stars, Gordon breaks away to build his own name, and Heston rewrites the rules as huge success brings both fame and a new world of pressure.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O’Connell.

programme.title: Hell or High Water
programme.desc: Film thriller. A divorced father and his ex-con older brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's ranch in west Texas.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: It’s the first quarter-final, and the four chefs who have fought their way through the heats return to the kitchen with everything to play for.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the northernmost reaches of the UK – Shetland – to fish the lochs and the seas of this remote and beautiful place for trout and pollock. Shetland is an archipelago of about 100 islands off the north east coast of Scotland, only around 15 of which are inhabited. It feels like they have entered a very different world - and it's full of surprises for both of them.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Bioacoustics technology and AI have allowed scientists to not only decode complex animal sound data but also begin communicating with animals. While this may mean the salvation of countless animal species, the advent of inter-species communication could also have far-reaching risks for the ecosystem. In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.desc: Calum Clunie has been growing for the Fife veg and flower shows since he was 15 years old, and now he has an allotment in Leven that has dedicated to growing the largest leeks and most dazzling dahlias. Throughout a growing season, Calum let us in on his show-growing secrets as he grows giant onions and massive cabbages alongside stunning sweet peas and delightful dahlias. As a fitting end to the growing year, Calum hosts his own homegrown show in his grandparent’s back garden. It's a real family affair, and there is a visit from a special surprise judge.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team enter Border country as the Roadshow visits Manderston, near Berwick-upon-Tweed. Amongst the items featured are pieces from Queen Victoria's household, a gruesome man trap and Lord Palmer's collection of rare biscuit tins.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Rochester Cathedral in Kent. Antiques expert Elizabeth Talbot falls for a book of fairy tales illustrated by Arthur Rackham, and Adam Partridge discovers an elegant chiming Swiss pocket watch. Presenter Paul Martin meets one of the last remaining survivors of the Dunkirk evacuation during the Second World War.

programme.title: House of Games

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives as she’s joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the couple’s next dances.

programme.title: Feast of Football
programme.desc: The inside track on Welsh football.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage from Hampden as Scotland host North Macedonia in the Nations League.

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig samples some X-themed materials. With Zoe Lyons, Susan Calman, Laura Smyth and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Mums v Big Pharma
programme.desc: Two mums from north west England tell the story, based on their experience, of taking on a drugs company, doctors and the government, fighting a scandal that led to at least 20,000 babies being born disabled - the truly shocking scandal of sodium valproate. The film reveals, for the first time, the ‘David v Goliath’ battle as they search for answers and fight for justice for their children.

programme.title: Blue Story
programme.desc: A feature adaptation of Rapman's YouTube series about two young south London friends from different boroughs and their deepening relationships with gangs and girls.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: Desperate to recover their losses, the Phelans strike a deal with Ozzie Thompson. At Jamie and Melissa’s engagement party, Michael and Diana attempt to broker peace with the family. Meanwhile, Freddie spirals further out of Michael’s control.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and asks if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. As the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle invites Pancake onto his radio show but is cross when his accidental burps prove a hit. Pancake soon discovers that fame as ‘burping guy’ has its downsides.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad and Cosima both think they're the best at pranking. Their prank war quickly spirals out of control, until Big Lizard finally reveals Proxima's real pranking champion!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's bathtime! The ducklings are determined Weasy will get clean.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The Gnome Crystal Mine has ground to a halt, leaving the forest with no crystals, no power supply and melting ice lollies! The heroes are tasked with a quest to find out what has happened and to fix it. It turns out that a slimy beast named Smarg has made the mine her home. But with Hoofius’s fear of gunk getting the better of him, evicting the slippery Smarg is not going to be easy.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings use magic Chinese lanterns for sound and light shows.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a referee at a football match, and Frog sees how much a footballer is cheered for scoring a goal. He is desperate to score one himself, but can he get past Duck's red card?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko worries that Hattrem could be holding itself back for the sake of others.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The dark magic of Vexius has contaminated Alfea with a lethal residue. The Winx, together with Flora's parents, are searching for a cure to save the flora and fauna of the magic kingdom.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini and Abby go head-to-head in an epic Children in Need racing challenge, and Tyler West and Hacker make some delicious Pudsey Pizzas.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve seeks out deadly creatures in miniature, including Australia’s most beautiful spider, Oman’s deadly deathstalker scorpion and a bright blue beauty in Indonesia.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens, this time in south east Asia. Since the 19th century, western gardeners have loved tropical gardens. Monty visits the archetype - the mysterious Jim Thompson's Garden in Bangkok. He seeks something more authentic in the Royal Palace gardens and the floating gardens of the canals of Bangkok. In Bali, his preconceptions are challenged again. Is the western picture of the exotic garden a construct?

programme.title: Naturewatch

programme.desc: In a rare in-depth interview, Sir Rod Stewart and Penny Lancaster welcome Anita Rani into their home to discuss their lives, family, fame and faith, and how Christmases past and present have shaped them. Across an intimate fireside chat, Christmas crafting in a festive greenhouse and a stroll around the stunning grounds of their countryside home, they reflect on Rod’s rise to fame, Penny’s journey from model to special constable and festive traditions, including exchanging gifts with Elton John.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off some sensational breakfasts to kickstart your weekend, including granola and yoghurt cupcakes, a banana and peanut butter bake, and a crazy-but-delicious breakfast pizza.

programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and Conker are joined by amazing Irish dancer and Kidz Bop British Sign Language interpreter Maisie! She needs Buddy’s help to make something tasty for her dancer friends to top them up after their energetic rehearsals. The only food that can jump as high as Maisie can are pancakes! So, Buddy makes bright green spinach pancakes stacked between layers of ham and an oozy cheese sauce - delicious and sure to knock the socks off her dancer friends! She can have it ready to go before dance class and simply pop it in the oven when she gets home. Maisie teaches Buddy to fingerspell his name in British Sign Language, and he tries to walk in Maisie’s very fast footsteps as he has a go at Irish dancing. Join Buddy, Conker and Maisie as they make a pancake stack that’s flippin’ delicious and will be sure to put a spring in your step, too! You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.desc: It's a day out! Duggee and the Squirrels are off on an underwater adventure with Betty's dad in his submarine. They see all the wonders of the underwater world, including a giant sea stallion and some jazz fish. And to the Squirrels, all those coloured buttons that work the submarine are just as interesting as what is outside. Betty's dad has a tricky time amusing the Squirrels. Thank goodness for the school of fish!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Animated preschool series. Duggee puts his delicious homemade apple pie on the window sill to cool down, but the second his back is turned it's gone. Who took it? Can the Squirrels find out? Fortunately, Duggee has his detective badge - and there are some very small footprints to follow. The Squirrels go and find lots of clues to help Duggee solve the mystery. Being a detective is hard work!

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Fergus starts acting strangely when he catches beastly blight. The doctors know the cure, but Fergus dismisses their advice in favour of his own muddler traditions.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: When Pancake’s precious golden algae go missing, all the Piri friends fall under suspicion. Pancake turns detective and replays the evening - but the solution is far from obvious!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wishes for an escalator to reach the top of a mini-mountain but soon realises she’s missing all the fun along the way.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Chipmunk accidentally gets hit by a ball during a game of baseball. To make him feel better, the ducklings feed him popcorn. The Chipmunk pretends to be sick to get more and more privileges. Weasy has had enough!

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: Gobby's Car-Tastrophe! Team Spidey saves the desert.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Peso and Dashi help a flying fox mother and pup survive the heat in an Australian swamp.

programme.title: Knee High Spies
programme.desc: Moss confronts her fear of the dark as Pranksy tries to spook the kids at their campout.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes go on an underwater adventure inside a rubbery bubble.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea plunges Broccoli and Carrot into the doughnut toppings simultaneously, and Supertato almost quits being a superhero when he can’t save his two friends at the same time.

programme.title: Gigglebiz
programme.desc: Hapless DIY enthusiast DIY Dan attempts to make a potted plant display. Rapids Johnson tries out a new technique to find a bear in the woods - it's called 'the bear sense'. Storybook Stan nearly gets blown away when he reads a story about a windy day and the wind keeps blowing in Arthur Sleep's news studio. Gardener Will Barrow is busy sweeping up leaves but the tidy piles are the perfect place for those cheeky animals to hide. The Lost Pirate is convinced that the bus stop is the place to wait for his ship. Roving reporter Gail Force discovers that she is a day late for the village fete she was booked to open. Captain Adorable tries to demonstrate his super mind power to Awesome Girl. Priscilla, the very noisy goose at Nana Knickerbocker's panto farm shop, refuses to lay a golden egg for a customer.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge thinks he's having a brilliant day. Everything seems to be going just right for him.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Banoffee pie was thought to have been invented in Sussex, and today Sonny-Mac is showing us how to make it. Sonny-Mac puts bananas and cream on top of a tasty base of crushed biscuits. He also adds his special ingredient, dates, to make it lovely and sweet. Not all his friends like the taste of dates at first, so let’s hope they enjoy them when the pie is ready. Sonny-Mac serves the pie to his friends at a special tea party, where everyone dresses very smartly.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Isla and Novah go digging with Chatterpot to explore wiggly roots and find out how they help plants grow tall. They also discover that some are tasty too!

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are playing hide-and-seek. Murphi is so difficult to find that he comes out of hiding to help Rebecca make a cardboard tube tracker dog. The Mini Monsters make paper bag monsters, and Rebecca’s Grandpa calls to share his fishing frustrations. The Recycling Express brings a shoebox, inspiring a mega monster idea - a magnificent monster! And the Tiny Helpers are on hand to help make the hutch.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: PC Plum must find the bird eating his prized strawberries. With Ava’s bird translator, he discovers it’s a chiffchaff and, after making friends with the bird, decides to share.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels go to see what Duggee is doing, but on the way Tag stumbles on some toy blocks and hurts his knee. How can they make him feel better? Happy's mum always says laughter is the best medicine. But how will they make Tag laugh? A-woof... maybe Duggee can help, he does have his comedy badge!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: The Octonauts evacuate the creatures living around a reef before a large archway collapses, but one stubborn convict fish refuses to move from her burrow.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny gets a tummy ache from not washing his hands, so Vida teaches him all about germs - and helps his tummy!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: When Xuli tries to beat Ubercorn's flying record, she accidentally damages a sea arch that holds up a rock formation. Inspired by Xuli's piloting skills, Tala convinces her to show her some tricks in the Grimbler, but disaster strikes when Tala traps herself under the fragile arch. The Go Jetters must race to save the day before the arch collapses.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Big Lizard isn't happy in his skin! Cosima tries everything to stop him scratching until she realises that's exactly what he needs to do. He's shedding his skin!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Yukee’s bouncing ball sets off a musical chain of events without anyone saying a word!

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button compete in their own Froggie sports day.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble tidies up his bedroom. Meanwhile, Justin and his friends play in a recycling band!

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Worm farmer Heather and the Fact Pack get hands-on with wiggly worms! We learn how wonderful worms help plants grow.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: When Ava’s dad can’t lead the Balamory Games, she searches for a new chieftain. But then Dynamite the Gladiator surprises her by placing the chieftain’s hat upon Ava’s head.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors become teachers at Dragon School for the day. Zog gets distracted entertaining the dragons and puts Pearl in danger of catching arcticosis, a deep-freeze condition.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Chloe tries to teach her dad a game she learnt at Bluey's house.

programme.title: MaeBee
programme.desc: Mae and Bee encourage their friend Tiger - a blind witch’s cat - to trust his senses and find his lost place in the treetops, and bring the spark back to his magic whiskers.

programme.title: Tralala
programme.desc: Tralala finds a secret life under the sofa which must be saved from the vacuum cleaner.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to swim with both her dads, but Jake feels nervous in the pool. Rafi makes a wish, and suddenly they all have mermaid tails! Jake isn’t sure at first, but with Rafi’s help, he learns to flip his tail and swim. When the wish ends, Jake is back on his feet and feels braver than before. Rafi understands that everyone gains courage in their own time, and the family share a happy hug.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick tells his grandson Remie about Barbara, an old school friend. She used to be big and bad, but only because someone was being big and bad to her.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: Love Monster visits Dr Piggles on Ha Ha Ha Day, only to find that his friend has the hiccups and is unable to make his patients laugh. Dr Piggles asks Love Monster if he can fill in for him while he rests, assuring him that he'll be right there to help out. But when the hiccups get worse, he has to lock himself in the back room, and Love Monster must find ways to make all the patients laugh by himself.

programme.title: Topsy and Tim
programme.desc: A hole in the roof means rain water is leaking in through the ceiling of Topsy and Tim's bedroom, making Topsy's top bunk and Little Moon Bunny wet. Tim helps Dad mend the leak with some help from Kerry's dad, Carson.

programme.title: Dylan's Playtime Adventures
programme.desc: Dylan the fashion designer wants to create the most special, brand new look ever - but coming up with that look is a lot harder than he thought!

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The Piggies decide to help Keith play with his ball, but their failed attempts lead to more and more repairs for the neighbours. Things get so bad that Wilf ends up confiscating the ball. Keith isn't allowed to play any more? Now, that is impossible!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Twinkle discovers an army of marching ants taking seeds from her vegetable garden. When all attempts to stop them fail, can she and Yukee find a way to get the ants marching to a different beat and away from her garden?

programme.title: Magic Hands
programme.desc: Look at what my hands can do! Bobbles dresses as Beowulf and meets some beastly creatures at the bottom of the sea. Simon and Donna go deep beneath the waves where they encounter Sheba the Snake dressed up as a horrible, scary sea monster. Thankfully, brave Bobbles saves the day as Beowulf complete with armour, helmet and a magical giant sword.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Mara visits the clinic with an unusually curly fin, but the doctors don’t agree on the diagnosis. Can Zog reunite Pearl and Gadabout so that they work together on the cure?

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo tells Dad about a new kid at kindy who is mean to her. Mum offers some good advice.

programme.title: Andy and the Band: Rock Star School
programme.desc: Andy and the Band take on their new roles as teachers at Rock Star School but soon realise this is no ordinary school. With the help of the talented Rock Star School kids, they soon find themselves on a mission solving mysteries in a world of magic, music and aliens!

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran spot a bird’s nest in Cynthia’s garden, which inspires JoJo to make a nest for Panda. Cynthia and Gran Gran teach JoJo about all the nests that different birds make to help their babies. Gran Gran has a plan: while JoJo waits for the eggs they found to hatch, they can go to the park and see all the ducklings that have already hatched out and about! Meanwhile, Daddy helps teach JoJo how to whistle just like a bird. After lots of tries, JoJo is finally whistling away! Soon, back at Cynthia’s, there’s a lovely surprise - the eggs have hatched.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Flynne helps Oona find Mossy, and proves she can be a friendly fox.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Charlie loves his little sister Lola, even if she gets carried away by her imagination sometimes! Charlie wins first prize at school for his fantastic homemade rocket. He tells Lola that the rocket is not a toy and that she must promise not to touch or play with it. When Lola and her imaginary friend Soren Lorenson find they have to transport an elephant back to the jungle, Soren persuades Lola that using the rocket is a really good idea.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: A relaxing, magical show about a lovely group of handmade toys who come to life at night. Join Pepi Nana and Moon Baby on their gentle adventures to the land of stories.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa have fun pretending to be different animals and making animal noises. At the Play Tree, they play with Purple Ducky and love making it squeak. When the squeak breaks, MeMo wants to find another toy to play with, but BaBa shows MeMo that they can still play with Purple Ducky. They take it to see the Yummies and their friends on the Lullaby Lake.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read bedtime stories. The Pontipines ride on the Ninky Nonk, but Mr and Mrs Pontipine can't find the children. It turns out those naughty dollies are riding on the roof of the Pontipine carriage.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: James Norton reads a very special story, about a little boy with a mammoth problem that he learns to manage.
